correctness.rationale: The state counts partition all available edges without overlap; the rational recurrence has explicit base cases. The potential drift identity and second-factorial-moment bound are proved symbolically for arbitrary valid states, yielding 0<=2/(n+1)-q_n<=4exp(pi^2/3)(H_{n+1}-H_2)/[n(n-1)]. Independent labeled-state enumeration, small full edge-order enumeration and rational drift identities reproduce the claim. Numerics are auxiliary; the proof applies to every n>=2.

The full-text 2024 local-limit theorem estimates densities of greedy independent sets under appropriate local convergence hypotheses. It does not state the exact finite crown recurrence and sharp rare-defect constant.

Accessible prior description of a radius-two-tree random matching law concerns forests, not crown graphs, which contain induced cycles for n>=3. The published chain-graph greedy MIS result addresses bipartite nested neighborhoods, while the crown graph has an induced 2K2 for n>=3 and is not a chain graph.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: None of these results has assumptions that specialize to, or conclusions strong enough to entail, an exact 2/n rare failure law for the complete-bipartite-minus-factor family. An exact matching/derangement enumeration counts matchings without weighting the random edge-order acceptance process and likewise cannot establish this claim by substitution.

value.rationale: Uniform random edge selection on the one-factor-deleted dense bipartite graph is a natural greedy-matching benchmark. All maximal matchings have either optimal size n or one-edge deficiency, so the exact deficiency probability is an intrinsic, meaningful performance statistic. Its computable all-order law and proved sharp coefficient 2/n distinguish it from generic approximation ratios or raw counts of perfect matchings; this is an infinite-family rare-event analysis, not a small computation.
